page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose compute instance powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor featuring 2 physical cores with hyperthreading for a total of 4 vCPUs. The instance is provisioned with 16 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Built on x86_64 architecture, the processor features 105 MB of L3 cache along with advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 extensions for targeted matrix and vector computing tasks. This instance includes no dedicated local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate solid single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core performance. Single-threaded performance tests, such as stress-ng single-core (1618.89) and Geekbench single-core (1713.0), demonstrate average performance levels, supported by single-threaded gzip compression at 26.37 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks show weak relative throughput, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 3315.66 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 3813.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth measures at 28.42 GB/sec for reads and 21.13 GB/sec for writes.

The instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for single-threaded tasks and light web traffic without requiring high memory bandwidth or local ephemeral disk space. Static web serving reaches an average throughput of 6.68 GB/sec, while small model LLM text generation achieves 112.11 tokens/sec. Given its physical core count of two and absence of local storage, the instance is best suited for entry-level microservices, general web serving, light API gateways, and single-threaded data processing workloads where dedicated CPU access is preferred over dense multi-threaded parallelism.
